$comment: THE VENDOR LICENCE TRUST ANCHOR.
WHAT THIS FILE IS. The PUBLIC half of the ToolsEnabled licence signing
keypair. It answers exactly one question: 'which key is allowed to say a
ToolsEnabled licence is genuine'. src/lib/providers/license.js pins licence
verification to this key and REFUSES -- LICENSE_TRUST_ANCHOR_MISSING -- when
this file is absent or carries no key. It never falls back to a locally held
key, because a machine that holds the private half of the key it trusts can
mint its own paid licence, which is the defect this anchor closes.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT.
- It is NOT a secret. A public key is safe to ship, safe to read, safe to
publish, and safe to copy. That is the entire point of asymmetric
signing: possessing it lets you CHECK a signature and never FORGE one.
- It is NOT the signing key. The private half lives only in the vendor's
local DPAPI vault under toolsenabled_license_signing_key_v1, is never
printed, logged, committed, or included in any shipped payload, and is
the only thing that can issue a licence.
- It is NOT a licence, an entitlement, or proof that this installation has
bought anything. An installation with no licence is fully functional
forever (src/lib/entitlement.js UNLICENSED_INSTALL). This file changes
nothing for such an installation.
- It is NOT a configurable trust setting. There is deliberately no
environment variable, user-data-directory override, or CLI flag that can
point verification at a different key: anything a customer's machine can
set is not an anchor, and letting absence of this file mean 'trust
anything' would reopen the hole by a different door.
ROTATION. Replacing the key here invalidates every licence signed by the
previous one, so it is a deliberate vendor act, not a maintenance chore. The
ceremony is createSigningKey({confirm:true}) in src/lib/providers/license.js;
it refuses to overwrite an existing signing key, so a rotation means
deleting the vault key first, on purpose.
PROVENANCE OF THIS KEY. Created 2026-08-11 by the deliberate ceremony. It
REPLACED an earlier key that this vault held by accident: the pre-fix
issueKey() generated and persisted a signing key whenever the vault had
none, so the key sitting here was minted as a side effect of an
attack-reproduction run rather than by any ceremony, and had already signed
a token. A vendor identity that nobody deliberately created is not a vendor
identity, so it was rotated out rather than pinned.
keyId is redundant with publicKeyPem on purpose. license.js recomputes it
from the key and REFUSES if the two disagree, so a hand-edit that swaps one
without the other fails loudly instead of quietly changing who is trusted.
